title: nchoosek
summary: Return a binomial coefficient or all k-combinations of a vector.

gpu_support.notes: gpuArray inputs are gathered before host-side coefficient calculation or combination materialization.

description: `nchoosek(n, k)` returns the binomial coefficient for selecting `k` items from scalar `n`. `nchoosek(v, k)` returns a matrix whose rows contain every `k`-element combination from vector `v` in input order.
behaviors: Scalar coefficient mode accepts nonnegative integer numeric scalars. `n` and `k` must have the same type unless one input is double, and mixed double/nondouble inputs return the nondouble class when the result fits.
Vector mode accepts numeric, complex, logical, and character vectors, including row vectors, column vectors, and empty vectors.
For vector inputs, the output has `k` columns and one row per combination.
When `k` is greater than the vector length, vector mode returns a 0-by-k empty matrix.
Unsupported containers such as string arrays, cells, structs, objects, and sparse arrays raise an input error.

examples.description: List combinations from a numeric vector

faqs.question: Does `nchoosek` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No GPU kernel is launched. RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs and materializes the scalar or combinations matrix on the host.

faqs.question: Why can `nchoosek(v, k)` fail for large vectors?
faqs.answer: The number of output rows grows combinatorially. RunMat rejects outputs that exceed its materialization limit rather than attempting an impractically large allocation.

gpu_residency: The result is a host value.
gpu_behavior: GPU inputs are gathered; no GPU kernels are launched.
